nextRevision.basis: The 22 May 2026 notification sets the variable dearness allowance once a year, from 1 April, from the average consumer price index of the previous calendar year, so the next VDA is due on 1 April 2027. No October revision is due.

sources.title: Revised minimum rates of wages for scheduled employments (single notification)
sources.legalBasis: Minimum Wages Act, 1948, sections 3(1)(b) and 5(1)(b), continued by section 69 of the Code on Wages, 2019. Karnataka Gazette (Extraordinary) Part IVA No. 389, 25 May 2026. In force from 22 May 2026; challenged in the Karnataka High Court (WP 16145/2026), which refused employers interim relief in September 2026 and stayed government circulars that had held back the new rates. A Cabinet sub-committee formed in August 2026 is reviewing the notification; no decision had been reported by 31 October 2026.

tables.appliesTo: The 61 employments in Annexure 1 and the 18 added to the schedule in Annexure 3 of the 22 May 2026 notification, including engineering and fabrication, automobile engineering, construction, shops and commercial establishments, hotels, hospitals, security and office staff through agencies, e-commerce and courier, and any employment not in the schedule. Annexure 2 sets higher rates for scavenging, power plants, foundries and fertiliser and pesticide units, and 19 piece-rated employments, including garments, agriculture and plantations, keep their earlier notifications until a committee revises them.

tables.vdaNote: The notification fixes the basic rates and a variable DA of 4 paise a day for each consumer price index point above 9,469, worked out every 1 April. The Labour Commissioner's summary sheet puts it at ₹1,030.80 a month (₹39.64 a day) from 22 May 2026. The monthly and daily figures here are the basic rate plus that VDA.

verification: 2026-10-16: karmikaspandana.karnataka.gov.in 'Minimum Wages Final Notification' lists the single notification LD 411 LWA 2023 dated 22.05.2026 (Gazette Part IVA No. 389, 25 May 2026), in force from 22 May 2026.

2026-10-16: Rates read from the gazette's Annexure 4 page images (the Kannada text layer is garbled) and from the department's English summary sheet. Zone 1 basic: highly skilled 31114.02 (1196.69 a day), skilled 28285.47 (1087.90), semi-skilled 25714.07 (989.00), unskilled 23376.43 (899.09); Zone 2 one step lower; Zone 3 two steps lower. VDA: 859 points x 0.04 x 30 = 1030.80 a month, 39.64 a day, payable from 22-05-2026.

2026-10-16, resolved 2026-10-31: Zone 3 unskilled basic reads 19319.36 in the gazette image and 19319.35 in the summary sheet's (poorly scanned) text layer. Re-read 2026-10-31 from a 400 dpi render of the sheet's image: it prints 19319.36, so 19319.35 was an OCR error in the text layer. 19319.36 is used (21251.30 / 1.1 = 19319.36).

2026-10-16, confirmed 2026-10-31: the gazette prints basic rates and the VDA separately, with no total column. Gazette page 9, condition 1, sets a variable DA of 4 paise a day for each CPI point above 9469 for all categories, worked out each 1 April from the previous calendar year's average (monthly VDA = points x rate x 30), so the Annexure 4 figures are basic and the VDA is added on top. The department's summary sheet ('Payable VDA Rs. 1030.80/- from 22-05-2026') gives the amount; the gazette gives only the formula. The monthly figures here add them.

2026-10-16: The notification is challenged in the Karnataka High Court (WP 16145/2026 with WA 1684-1685/2026). Reports (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench, not primary) say interim relief was refused around 21 Sep 2026 and the circulars of 29 Jul and 10 Aug 2026 deferring the rates were stayed on 18 Sep 2026.

2026-10-31: court status update (news reports, not primary). LiveLaw (21 September 2026): Justice H.T. Narendra Prasad refused interim protection in WP 16145/2026 (Karnataka Employers' Association); he first ordered the petitions heard with WA 1684-1685/2026, then reversed that the same evening because the Division Bench had reserved judgment in those appeals. Deccan Herald and Bar & Bench (19 September 2026): on 18 September the court stayed three circulars, from the Directorate of Municipal Administration, the Panchayat Raj Department and the State Audit and Accounts Department, that deferred the rates for outsourced and contract workers. Urban Acres and LegalSuvidha (17 October 2026, not confirmed by mainstream outlets) report a stay around 16 October of a 9 October 2026 circular that kept urban development and town planning staff on old wages. The Hans India (20 August 2026): a Cabinet sub-committee under G. Parameshwara was formed on 13 August to examine the notification; no decision reported. No stay of the 22 May 2026 notification and no final judgment found. Listing karmikaspandana.karnataka.gov.in/47/ still ends at the two 22-05-2026 entries; both cited PDFs re-downloaded with matching sha256.

2026-11-02: Read the whole 22 May 2026 gazette (24 pages, Kannada) from 300 dpi renders. Its preamble says Karnataka had fixed rates for 81 scheduled employments by separate notifications and that the 11 April 2025 draft covered 99. The final notification has four parts: Annexure 1 (61 employments already in the schedule, item 20 being any employment not in the schedule) and Annexure 3 (18 added to the schedule) take the Annexure 4 zone rates; Annexure 2 sets its own rates for scavenging (one rate, Zone 1/2/3 basic 25714.07/23376.43/21251.30), power generation units (no zones: thermal 34225.42/31114.02/28285.47/25714.07, hydro, solar and wind 31114.02/28285.47/25714.07/23376.43 for highly skilled to unskilled) and foundries and chemical fertiliser and pesticide units (Zone 1/2/3 one step above Annexure 4); and a 'special note' leaves 19 piece-rated, labour-intensive employments to be revised by a committee under section 8(1)(a) of the Code (beedi, cashew, handloom and powerloom, loading and unloading, agarbatti, agriculture, forestry and timber depots, bricks, silk textiles, fish, coffee curing, two plantation schedules, spinning mills, garments and tailoring, cloth dyeing and printing, khadi and village industries, shamiana and pandal work, and MSMEs). The conditions, including the VDA, apply to Annexures 1, 2 and 3. Cleaning workers in any scheduled employment get the Annexure 2 rate. The page had shown Annexures 1 and 3 as 'most scheduled employments' and left out power plants and the 19.

2026-11-02: karmikaspandana.karnataka.gov.in/64/ ('Minimum Wages rates for the Year 2026-27', uploaded about 24 March 2026) lists 81 rate sheets, one per employment, each giving its notification, base points, the 2026-27 index (10,328) and basic + VDA = total from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027. It has sheets for 16 of the 19 committee employments; khadi, shamiana and MSMEs have none. The single notification does not touch the 19, so these sheets are their current rates. All 16 were transcribed from 200-300 dpi page images (text layers are OCR'd and unreliable) and basic + VDA = total was checked on every row. The VDA on every sheet is points x the notification's rate (4 paise; 3 for beedi) x 30 a month, and that / 26 a day.

2026-11-02: printed quirks kept as printed: beedi skilled, semi-skilled and unskilled day totals are a paisa below basic + VDA (worked from month / 26); fish row 5 prints row 4's monthly figures although its day rate is lower; garments skilled Zone III day total 518.69 (basic + VDA 518.68); spinning skilled Zone II day total 534.46 (534.47); loading's 178 for distributing a 70-200 litre container is far above its column; handloom's saree table prints an unlabelled 27.3 (left out); bricks prints single figures for task and piece work without a unit; cashew prints no rate for hand shellers with electricity; agarbatti's pouch row reads 'more than 171 grams to 50 grams'. Several notifications take effect before their date (silk, spinning and dyeing from 30 December 2017 by a 17 January 2023 notification; beedi from 1 April 2024 by one of 27 February 2025).
